questions.q: Why can't navigation in Lightning Experience generally be handled with a plain, hardcoded `<a href="...">` link?
options: Lightning Experience is a single-page app without stable, predictable URLs to hardcode, so a plain link would bypass the app's own routing and state management
Anchor tags are not supported inside LWC templates at all
href attributes can only point to external websites, never to internal Salesforce records
Only Aura components are allowed to use anchor tags
questions.explain: Because Lightning Experience manages its own routing and state as a single-page application, a hardcoded link would bypass that routing -- which is exactly why lightning/navigation exists as a dedicated service.

questions.q: How is navigation functionality applied to a component's class?
options: By decorating a method with @navigate
By importing a global navigate() function and calling it directly with no setup
By applying the NavigationMixin to the component's base class: `extends NavigationMixin(LightningElement)`
Navigation requires no explicit setup; every component can navigate by default
questions.explain: NavigationMixin is a mixin applied to the component's base class, not a decorator or a plain function import -- its methods are then accessed through the bracket syntax on `this`.

questions.q: What does a `standard__recordPage` PageReference's `attributes` typically include?
options: Only a `url` property
Only a `pageName` property
A `recordId`, an `objectApiName`, and an `actionName`
A list of fields to display on the record
questions.explain: standard__recordPage navigates to a specific record's view/edit/clone page, and its attributes are recordId, objectApiName, and actionName (such as 'view').

questions.q: What is the functional difference between `NavigationMixin.Navigate` and `NavigationMixin.GenerateUrl`?
options: They are two names for the exact same behavior
Navigate can only be called from connectedCallback(), while GenerateUrl can be called from anywhere
GenerateUrl only works for external web pages, never for records
Navigate immediately moves the user to the target page; GenerateUrl returns a Promise resolving to the URL string without navigating anywhere
questions.explain: Navigate performs the actual navigation immediately. GenerateUrl instead resolves a Promise with the URL string, useful for populating a real href without navigating, letting the user middle-click or right-click the link naturally.

questions.q: Why is pairing GenerateUrl (for a real href) with Navigate (called from a click handler) a common recommended pattern?
options: Because GenerateUrl alone cannot produce a valid URL string
Because Navigate requires a href attribute to already exist on the element
Because it gives a real href for accessibility and native browser behaviors like opening in a new tab, while still routing normal clicks through the in-app Navigate call via event.preventDefault()
Because GenerateUrl and Navigate must always be called together or neither will work
questions.explain: A real href (from GenerateUrl) supports native link behaviors like opening in a new tab. Calling Navigate from the click handler, after preventDefault(), still lets the in-app router handle a normal click correctly.
